title: Resume Tailor
summary: A web app that rewrites your resume for a specific job posting with Claude, using only experience already on your resume. Now being rebuilt as an agent that checks every line against your resume.
highlights: 97 tests and CI on every pull request, with the app split into tested services
MCP server with four tools for job posts, company research, resumes, and past applications
Eval suite comparing the single-call baseline, the agent, and the agent with the grounding check, with Wilson intervals
OpenTelemetry tracing across the agent loop and a live demo script that runs with no API key
problem: Tailoring your resume to every job posting takes a long time. Language models can do it in seconds, but they tend to add skills and numbers you never had. A tailored resume is only useful if every line on it is true.
built: You paste in your resume and a job posting, or a link to one. The app reorders and rewords your experience to match the role, writes a matching cover letter, and shows which keywords from the posting your resume is missing.

The first version makes one model call per feature. The rebuild turns it into an agent with tools, a check that traces every output line back to your original resume, and an eval suite that measures how often it invents something.

milestones.name: MCP server with tools for job posts, company research, and resumes
Agent loop that plans and calls the tools
Grounding check that flags invented experience
Eval suite comparing baseline, agent, and agent with the check

title: JudgeCheck
summary: A toolkit for checking whether LLM judges are reliable. It loads JSONL and LangSmith trace exports into one shared record type for scoring.
problem: An LLM judge can score a good answer as bad and sound confident doing it. Before you trust a judge, you need to know how reliable it is.
built: It loads JSONL trace files and LangSmith dataset exports into one shared record type, so the same traces can be scored by any judge.

Two judges score each trace through the same Judge protocol: one for relevance and one for grounding. Each takes a trace and returns a verdict plus a rationale, with the prompt and model configurable.
highlights: Reliability checks: perturbation stability and cross-judge agreement with Cohen's kappa
33 tests and CI on every pull request
Two configurable LLM judges that score traces for relevance and grounding
Statistics with Wilson intervals and Cohen's kappa

decisions.title: One shared TraceRecord for every loader
decisions.body: Judges and reliability checks should only ever see one shape. The loaders own the messy mapping from each source format, and everything after ingestion works with the same fields.

decisions.title: MalformedTraceError for bad traces
decisions.body: One named error type lets callers catch exactly this failure, and failing the whole load with the file and line number makes a bad trace easy to find and fix. Raising instead of skipping keeps the trace count honest.

decisions.title: One Judge protocol with prompt and model set at construction
decisions.body: Every judge implements one protocol: one method that takes a trace and returns a verdict plus a rationale. Prompt and model are set at construction, the API key comes from the environment, and a client can be injected so tests run offline.

milestones.name: Trace ingestion from JSONL and LangSmith
Statistics with Wilson intervals and Cohen's kappa
